title: Coherence of the higher direct images
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation and $\cF$ an
$\cO_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $T$ (the standing
assumptions of this subsubsection). Then:

- **(a)** For every $g:T'\to T$, with $f':X'\to T'$ and $\cF'$ the base
changes of $f$ and $\cF$, the base change map
$Lg^*Rf_*\cF\to Rf'_*\cF'$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of
$\cO_{T'}$-modules. Moreover $Rf_*\cF$ is locally computed by finite free
complexes ([lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex]): every
point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ and an integer $d_U\ge0$ with a
complex $P$ of finite free $\cO_U$-modules concentrated in degrees
$[0,d_U]$ such that for every $g:T'\to U$, with
$f':X'\to T'$ and $\cF'$ the base changes of $f$ and $\cF$, one has
$H^q(g^*P)\cong R^qf'_*\cF'$ for all $q$. In particular
$R^qf_*\cF|_U=0$ for all $q>d_U$.
- **(b)** If $T$ is locally Noetherian, $R^qf_*\cF$ is a coherent
$\cO_T$-module for all $q$; for this, flatness of $\cF$ over $T$ is not
needed. If $T$ is locally Noetherian and $\cF$ is flat over $T$, then
$Rf_*\cF$ is perfect: locally on $T$ it is represented by a bounded complex
of finite locally free modules.
- **(c)** If $T$ is quasi-compact, $R^qf_*\cF=0$ for all $q\gg0$.

proof.text: For (a), apply [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] with $S=T$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$. Its properness, finite-presentation and relative-flatness hypotheses are exactly the standing assumptions. It identifies the canonical derived-to-ordinary module base-change map as an isomorphism for every $g:T'\to T$. In particular this is the specified map, not just an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

Apply [lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex] at each $t\in T$. It supplies $U$, $d_U$ and a complex $P$ supported in $[0,d_U]$, together with $H^q(g^*P)\cong R^qf'_*\mathcal F'$ for every base change into $U$. Taking $g=\mathrm{id}_U$, the base change of $f$ along the open immersion $U\subseteq T$ is $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ with the restriction of $\mathcal F$, and [lem-pc-sections-open-base-change] identifies its $q$-th higher direct image with $(R^qf_*\mathcal F)|_U$; hence $H^q(P)\cong(R^qf_*\mathcal F)|_U$ for all $q$. For $q>d_U$, both $P^q$ and its next term are zero, so its cycles and therefore $H^q(P)$ are zero. This proves the local vanishing $(R^qf_*\mathcal F)|_U=0$ in (a).

proof.text: For the coherence assertion of (b), drop relative flatness. Properness implies finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $X$ locally Noetherian. The finite presentation of $\mathcal F$ implies quasi-coherence by clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], and implies finite type by its local finite presentation: the finitely many target basis vectors generate the cokernel [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Hence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal F$ coherent. Now [lem-pc-coherent-hi] applies to this proper morphism over locally Noetherian $T$ and gives coherence of every $R^qf_*\mathcal F$. No step here uses flatness.

proof.text: When relative flatness is restored, [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] also gives that $Rf_*\mathcal F$ is perfect, in particular when $T$ is locally Noetherian. By [def-pc-perfect-complex], on an affine open it is represented by a bounded complex $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ of finite projective modules. Each $P^i$ is a direct summand of a finite free module; localizing its inclusion and retraction preserves their identity composite. Thus each principal localization is finite projective, and [lem-sc-principal-open-finite-projective-tilde] with the whole affine open as $U$ says that every term $\widetilde{P^i}$ is finite locally free. This is the local representative asserted in (b).

For (c), the neighbourhoods $U_t$ from step 2 cover $T$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_s$. Put $N=\max(\{0,d_{U_1},\ldots,d_{U_s}\})$. If $q>N$, the sheaf $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ restricts to zero on each $U_j$. Two sections on any open set have equal restrictions on its intersections with these $U_j$, and hence are equal by the sheaf separation axiom. Thus every section module is zero and $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$. If $T$ is empty, the empty subcover and $N=0$ give the same conclusion.
